title: Lentil and Mushroom Salad
subtitle: Puy lentils with sauteed chestnut mushrooms, thyme and red wine vinegar
excerpt: Earthy Puy lentils combined with sauteed chestnut mushrooms, shallots and thyme, dressed in a red wine vinegar dressing. A deeply savoury, meat-free salad that works warm or cold.
sourceNotes: Lentil and mushroom combinations appear across European peasant cooking traditions, where both ingredients were affordable, nutritious and available through winter. The salad format, with a sharp vinegar dressing, is most closely associated with French and Italian grain salad traditions. The specific combination of Puy lentils with chestnut mushrooms and thyme is characteristic of modern British vegetarian cooking from the 1990s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the lentils a day ahead. Saute the mushrooms fresh before serving.

content.text: Lentil and mushroom salad is deeply savoury and satisfying in a way that many vegetable salads are not. Both lentils and mushrooms carry umami, and the red wine vinegar dressing sharpens the whole dish. The mushrooms need to be cooked at high heat to colour rather than steam; colour is where the flavour is. Add them to the lentils while still warm.
Cover {{puy-lentils}} of Puy lentils with cold water by 5 cm. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until just tender. Drain and season with salt while warm.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the shallots and cook for 2 minutes. Add the {{mushrooms-chestnut}} of mushrooms in a single layer (do this in two batches if the pan is crowded) and cook without stirring for 2 to 3 minutes until golden underneath. Toss, add the {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and the thyme leaves, cook for another minute. Season with salt and pepper.

Whisk together {{red-wine-vinegar}} of red wine vinegar, the extra-virgin olive oil, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the warm lentils and toss. Add the mushrooms and parsley and toss again. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough, or too many mushrooms at once.
items.fix: Cook in batches in a very hot pan. Mushrooms are mostly water; they need high heat to evaporate that moisture and brown. Crowding releases steam and they stew.
Season the lentils assertively right out of the water, and season the mushrooms in the pan. Both need salt at the cooking stage, not just in the dressing.

content.text: Lentil and mushroom salad belongs to the autumn and winter repertoire: both ingredients are at their best (or at least most appropriate) when the weather turns cold. It appeared in British vegetarian cooking in the 1990s and became a bistro staple. Unlike many grain salads it holds its flavour at room temperature, which makes it a practical choice for buffets and advance preparation.
